answer: Each blade leaves the cutler's shop stamped with the maker's mark, and the stamp register holds the mark of every blade sold that year. A meadow blade ground in another town fails the register: at the glacier of the stamp the letters must match the cutler's own punch, and a strange blade carries no stamp at all. Faking a blade means buying a forge, hiring a grinder and paying 8,200, while the opal entry in the register is read at every market, so a blade whose stamp repeats is seized.
